title: CORE-7119 · SHARED: bold body text too light (#595959 vs live #313131)
body:
**Linear:** [CORE-7119](https://linear.app/bsq-group/issue/CORE-7119/rf-shared-bold-body-text-too-light-595959-vs-live-313131) · state `In Progress` · priority P3

## Ticket (verbatim from Linear)

**Component/area:** body rich-text bold run — `.payload-richtext strong` / `b`
**Breakpoints:** 360 / 768 / 1024 / 1800 — all four
**Live:** [https://www.rapidformations.co.uk/id-requirements/](<https://www.rapidformations.co.uk/id-requirements/>) · **Test:** [https://rapid-formations-clone.vercel.app/id-requirements](<https://rapid-formations-clone.vercel.app/id-requirements>)

### Issue

Live darkens bold runs inside body rich text (e.g. a "Note:" lead-in) to `#313131`, distinguishing them from the surrounding `#595959` paragraph text. On the clone, bold runs inside body copy simply inherit the paragraph colour, so they only differ by weight and read flatter than live. This is a shared body rich-text styling defect (`.payload-richtext strong`/`b`), not a content issue — the token itself already exists and renders correctly elsewhere on the clone.

### Impacted pages

**Confirmed affected:**

| Page | Bold run(s) | Live | Clone |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `/id-requirements/` | "Note:" | `#313131` | `#595959` |
| `/director-appointment-resignation/` | "Please note:" | `#313131` | `#595959` |
| `/whistleblowing-grievance-mechanism-policy/` | 7 list lead-ins | `#313131` | `#595959` |
| `/vat-registration/` | "Buy Now" | `#313131` | `#595959` |
| `/additional-services/business-address/` | "Buy Now" | `#313131` | `#595959` |
| `/additional-services/london-registered-office/` | "Buy Now" | `#313131` | `#595959` |
| `/additional-services/service-address/` | "Buy Now" | `#313131` | `#595959` |
| `/business-telephone/` | "Improve your corporate image" | `#313131` | `#595959` |
| `/terms-and-conditions/` | 338 clause references | `#313131` | `#363636` (wrong value applied, not missing) |

**Confirmed unaffected** (bold already renders `#313131` correctly, do not regress): `/ico-registration/` (4 bold runs, feature-list style), and the "Enhance your corporate image..." bold run on `/business-telephone/`. Review-figure bold ("4.8"/"4.9") is `#595959` on both sites and is correct as-is.

**Also checked, no bold present / not applicable:** `/transfer-of-shares/`, `/company-dissolution/`, `/issue-of-shares/`, `/confirmation-statement-service/`, `/company-name-change/`, `/dormant-company-accounts/`, `/psc-filing/`.

Many RF pages aren't built on the clone yet, so this list may grow as those go live — not claiming sitewide beyond what's confirmed above.

### Expected vs actual

|  | Expected (Live) | Actual (Clone) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| bold run `color` | `#313131` | `#595959` (`#363636` on `/terms-and-conditions/`) |
| paragraph `color` | `#595959` | `#595959` |
| `font-weight` / size / line-height | 700 / 20px / 30px | match — identical to live |

Colour is the only mismatch; weight, size, and line-height already match on all four breakpoints.

### Scope / implementation constraint

* Fix must target the body rich-text bold selector specifically — not a global `<strong>`/`<b>` rule.
* Do not apply to bold inside headings: live keeps bold inside `<h2>`/`<h3>` at `#595959` (see `/cookies-policy/`, [CORE-7120](<https://linear.app/bsq-group/issue/CORE-7120>)) — a blanket darken-all-bold rule would break that.
* Do not regress bold contexts that already match live: `/ico-registration/` feature-list bold, the correct bold run on `/business-telephone/`, and the `#595959` review-figure bold.
* Must not affect body inline links, buttons, or header/footer bold text, which have their own colours.

### Definition of Done

- [ ] Bold runs inside body rich text render `#313131` at 360 / 768 / 1024 / 1800.
- [ ] Surrounding paragraph text stays `#595959`.
- [ ] Fixed on the shared body rich-text style, verified on `/id-requirements/`, `/director-appointment-resignation/`, `/whistleblowing-grievance-mechanism-policy/`, `/vat-registration/`, `/business-telephone/`, and `/terms-and-conditions/` (currently `#363636`, must also end up `#313131`).
- [ ] No regression to bold inside headings, or to already-correct bold contexts (`/ico-registration/`, review-figure bold, the correct run on `/business-telephone/`).
- [ ] No change to bold weight/size/line-height and no layout/wrapping shift.

### Evidence

Live-vs-clone screenshots (Note: lead-in + section context, all four breakpoints, plus the whistleblowing/T&Cs examples) are attached to this ticket.

---
### Routing note (Planning)
`rapid-formations-clone` has **no clone engine** — no `walk-dom-cdp.ts` / `emit-block.ts` /
`verify-clone.ts`, and zero `*Clone` blocks. Every block here is hand-authored, so the
engine-first rule has nothing to diagnose into: this is a **direct fix in the block that
has the defect**. That is why the task is tagged `bug` — it is NOT a fidelity loophole.

**Ship path:** Mode X — `clone-pull-request-create` with per-breakpoint PROD-vs-clone
screenshot proof, land `awaiting-user`, **the USER merges the PR**. Never merge to main.
Live source of truth: `https://www.rapidformations.co.uk` · clone:
`https://rapid-formations-clone.vercel.app`. ⛔ HEADED browser only for any visual check.
acceptanceCriteria: Bold runs inside body rich text render `#313131` at 360 / 768 / 1024 / 1800, via the shared `.payload-richtext strong`/`b` style — not a global `<strong>`/`<b>` rule.
Surrounding paragraph text stays `#595959`; bold weight/size/line-height unchanged and no layout/wrapping shift.

Verified on `/id-requirements/`, `/director-appointment-resignation/`, `/whistleblowing-grievance-mechanism-policy/`, `/vat-registration/`, `/business-telephone/` and `/terms-and-conditions/` (currently `#363636`, must also end up `#313131`).
No regression to bold inside headings — live keeps bold in `<h2>`/`<h3>` at `#595959` (see CORE-7120) — so a blanket darken-all-bold rule is not acceptable.
No regression to already-correct bold contexts: `/ico-registration/` feature-list bold, the correct run on `/business-telephone/`, and the `#595959` review-figure bold.
